title: The Shape of I
statement: I am not a single outline. I am a body located in a city, woven from inherited patterns, driven by thought, and open to strange forms of growth. The figure is centered, but the self is made from everything that surrounds and enters it.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

notes.error: Use a boolean done and at most 12 actions; an empty batch is allowed only when done is true or reviewOnly is true.

notes.note: Establish a grounded, layered self-portrait: the city map becomes the field, the drawn figure the vulnerable central self, with pattern, gears, and anemone forms expressing inheritance, thought, and inner life.

actions.title: The Shape of I
actions.statement: I am not a single outline. I am a body located in a city, woven from inherited patterns, driven by thought, and open to strange forms of growth. The figure is centered, but the self is made from everything that surrounds and enters it.

notes.note: The central figure is readable but quiet; add three contrasting forms around it to make the self feel active and relational without covering the portrait: insects as agency, fungi as growth, and a bridge as connection.

The collage already reads clearly as a self assembled from place, inheritance, mechanism, biology, and connection. Add one restrained circular architectural motif behind the figure to clarify the inward, first-person focus without obscuring the portrait.

The final canvas is balanced and legible: the centered figure is held by a map, framed by inherited pattern and architectural ornament, while machine, insect, anemone, fungi, and bridge forms expand the meaning of a self beyond a single body. Finish with the established title and statement.
